newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee range-bound on low dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee range-bound on low dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee was steady against the dollar in early Wednesday trading, due to a lack of commercial demand for the greenback and high call money rates, dealers said.
At 0445 GMT the rupee was quoted at its opening level of 58.35 to the dollar. The rupee closed at the same level on Tuesday.

"The rupee is not going to move without commercial demand for dollars," said a Commercial Bank dealer. "Speculators are silent due to the overseas weakness of the dollar and the likelihood that the Central Bank will push the currency down."
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar-rupee exchange rate by a quarter of a local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.3259 and 59.5042.
Overnight call money rates were at 13 percent, after opening at 14 percent, dealers said.
"Call rates rose when a number of foreign banks began borrowing," said a Hongkong and Shanghai Bank dealer.
Foreign banks which have limited branch networks, regularly borrow heavily on the call market, he said.
